answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance comes from progressive bonding on identity uniqueness. An attacker creating many fakes must pay the full cost of independently sustaining each—like planting a separate willow for every lagoon they invent—because ongoing original work cannot be shared. Each identity uses its own computational quill to produce graded attestations; the expense multiplies linearly with controlled accounts, while one honest agent pays only once. Behavioral clustering detection raises concealment costs further.
